market_holds: Spot $4.78 at the 2026-11-16 seal, 1% above the 52-week low and 67% below the high. Run-up is -8.1% over 5 days and -12.8% over 20 days; MTD -21.8% and YTD -56.9% (AAII, 2026-11-16). The stock was $8.93 on 2026-09-30, so it is down about 46% since Q3 ended, roughly the same as the neocloud group (CRWV -50%, NBIS -48% from Oct 6 to Nov 6, per secondary reports). Options price an event move of 14.1% (straddle 16.2%, ATM IV 165%), against a historical median reaction of 4.1% over 8 prints (5 down). Q3 consensus is revenue $12.8M and EPS -$0.01 (Earnings Whispers, 2026-11-10/16), double Q2's $6.18M; FY26 consensus is $55.5M. Coverage is thin, and the last several prints missed consensus. The company guide is FY26 revenue above $50M with positive adjusted EBITDA, reaffirmed by the new CFO on 2026-10-05, after the quarter closed and after the GPUaaS subsidiary was sold to Axe Compute on 2026-09-30, and repeated in the LD Micro deck of 2026-10-20. On the Q2 call (per secondary summaries) management guided Q4 recurring infrastructure revenue of $17-18M, a >$70M exit run rate and a 2027 framework of at least $160M. H1 revenue was $8.3M, so H2 must exceed $41.7M. Short interest is 6.25M shares on 2026-10-30, about 20% of the 31.3M shares outstanding at June 30, with 6.8 days to cover (Nasdaq API). Earnings Whispers records a -56% post-earnings drift since the August print.
view: This print turns on whether the >$50M FY26 guide survives and whether the colocation ramp (12 MW billed at Columbus by end of August, 10 MW hyperscaler capacity due in Q4, 55 MW Axe late 2026 to early 2027) is real revenue. Q3 itself matters less. The arithmetic is tight. H1 was $8.3M; with Q3 at the $12.8M consensus, Q4 needs about $29M against a recurring-infrastructure guide of $17-18M, so roughly $11-12M of Q4 Technology Solutions revenue (about $28M of 2026 backlog, only $3.8M recognized in H1) has to land. The sale of the GPU cluster to Axe at quarter end, with Duos leasing the capacity back and covering colo and energy for five years, also gives a CFO a reason to reshape the numbers: the GPUaaS line could be presented as discontinued or netted, and margins could compress. Against that, the same new CFO reaffirmed '>$50M' on 2026-10-05 knowing roughly what Q3 looked like, and repeated it on 2026-10-20. The stock already trades as if the story is broken: it has halved with the sector, sits at its low and carries a 20% short. A clean reaffirmation could produce a sharp squeeze, as CoreWeave's beat-and-raise did on 2026-11-10. A trim to 'approximately $50M' or a headline revenue miss (this company has missed thin consensus repeatedly) would extend the trend, and dilution for the 55 MW and 20 MW buildouts is an overhang that could appear with the print. I cannot see which branch the release takes; the evidence on each side is about the same size, with a slight tilt down from repeated misses, the Q4 load and the deal complexity.

recommendation.reason: I found no dated evidence that the price has not already absorbed. The stock is at its lows after a sector-wide 45-50% drawdown, with crowded shorts and a 14% implied move. The guide was reaffirmed after quarter end, but the Q4 arithmetic is tight and the company has a record of missing thin consensus. These pull in opposite directions with no decisive datum between them.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: An explicit reaffirmation of FY26 >$50M with Q3 revenue at or above $12.8M and Q4 recurring revenue confirmed at $17-18M would make me lean long, given 20% short interest. A cut or reshaped guide, or an equity raise announced with the print, would make me lean short.

self_critique: The case for long: the CFO, three weeks into the job, reaffirmed >$50M after Q3 closed and again at LD Micro, and a CFO who expected to cut would rarely do that twice. The stock is at its low with 20% short interest and a sector already rebounding on peer beats, so even an in-line print with the guide held could gap up 10-20% at the open. The case for short: the Q4 load, a structurally confusing quarter (cluster sale, discontinued-ops risk, colo and energy costs absorbed), repeated misses against thin consensus, and an obvious need for capital to build 55 MW plus 20 MW, which microcaps often raise right around a print. Neither case is strong enough to move me past 54% on either side.
